title: Consumer Protections for Artificial Intelligence
committees: House State, Civic, Military, and Veterans Affairs
last_action: Signed by the Governor and enacted as Chapter 198.
summary: Requires developers and deployers of high-risk AI systems to use reasonable care against known or reasonably foreseeable algorithmic-discrimination risks, publish specified disclosures, complete impact assessments, and report certain discovered risks.
committee_dynamics: Colorado enacted the first broad U.S. state framework centered on consequential high-risk systems; it is included as an adjacent, enforceable risk-management law.

deadlines.requirement: Developer and deployer duties become operative.

agency_status.detail: The operative date has passed; this starter record has not yet completed a rulemaking and enforcement inventory.

sources.title: SB24-205 Consumer Protections for Artificial Intelligence
